correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, K>1 and 1<t<K, Sherman–Morrison and scalar Rayleigh extrema prove the two unique non-tie divergence minima over all signed symmetric rank-one updates. Rank-one Weyl interlacing and Loewner order prove the universal spectral condition-number lower bound and explicit candidates attain it. The logarithmic-mean ordering and strictly monotone mismatched ratios give exact supremal factors. Seeded numerical verifier passed 9,093 checks; finite checks support but do not establish the quantified proof.

originality.rationale: Comparison of exact mathematical implications shows the published forward/reverse BLD scalar scores were already known, and the earlier PSD rank-constrained condition-number theorem does not cover an indefinite relative error. Neither inspected source establishes the two sharp logarithmic-mean selection thresholds together with the global all-rank-one spectral condition-number optimum and unbounded fixed-K competitive ratios. Search results were additionally screened for aliases and stronger related bounds; residual uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent logarithmic-mean spectral selection theorem could appear in earlier matrix-nearness or preconditioning literature under different terminology.
The later Kaporin/Bregman paper was accessible by abstract only, not inspected as full text; it discusses a different nominal condition-number metric.
A similarity search and focused literature inspection do not establish exhaustive absence of equivalent prior theorems.

value.rationale: The indefinite relative error naturally arises with approximate factorization preconditioners, and comparison of an optimization surrogate to the best condition number under the same rank budget is directly motivated by the source literature. The exact four-region logarithmic-mean phase diagram and sharp unbounded loss quantify a genuine structural boundary, over the full noncommuting rank-one correction class. This is not merely a scalar mode-score restatement, and it does not infer Krylov runtime from conditioning.
